persistedClaim.text: The UCAS personal statement moved from a single 4,000-character free-text box to a structured format.

record.text: Thank you, Sapna. So a very warm welcome to everyone. So and thank you for taking the time to get into this learning. And with the new changes in UCAS, it definitely helps us go do a quick run-through for the LOR. So when it comes to the letter of reference, as Sapna mentioned, it has the new format allows us to divide it into the three sections. One, the first section is around context, which talks more about the school. In this section, we can elaborate about the what type of school or the curriculum that is being offered at the school. Also, the school can talk about their academic environment, and in particular if there is a different assessment systems or any subject or qualification that are not offered in the school. This helps this information helps us understand about the applications education context. Again, here I would like to highlight if the school has a certain type of profile in terms of sending students or some sort of accomplishments around various universities, they can definitely mention that and give a little context around the school as well. The second part of the LOR is the extenuating circumstances. Now this is not very often this is utilized, but God forbid if there are circumstances, it's life, sometimes things happen which are beyond control. We should mention this in this section that can help us assess the applicant fairly. So sometimes these circumstances can be in the cases in the situation like a bereavement just around the LOR or just around when the applications were being made, any significant health illnesses. We have often seen now that people who have the diagnosis mention about ADHD or dyslexia diagnosis in their LOR section now. That helps us helps the admissions judge them fairly on their applications, etc. With regards to the third section, which is the most important highlight of the LOR, this is about the academic strength for the students, a potential course suitability, and a relevant contextual information for the student or like for the referee to elaborate. So please keep in mind that the LOR is around 4000 characters, roughly around 600 words. So this is the total sort of expectation, word expectation from the whole of the LOR, and we request people to stick to this this word limit. Now, in this third section, this is your most important section where we want to highlight the academic strength of the students. Now, there are often a lot of students who have done a lot of things and achieved a lot of different elements during their academic journey, but we have to find out and pick as a as a referee or as a counselor, we have to make sure we pick the ones that is most relevant to the subject they're applying to. So say particularly if it's a subject strength, if they've turned, if they've taken up any activity or have achieved a national rank in an Olympiad, things like that should be added in the third section. Can I request to go on the third, next slide, please? Yeah, this brings us to the first poll. What should be included in the first section of the LOR?

Sapna Goyal: Thank you, Rashi. Thank you for that amazing introduction. It's always a pleasure to be with the TOC. It's one of those opportunities, one of the places that I'm here because of the learning opportunities, as you mentioned. So can we start with the slide, Bijoya? The first one. The topic today, actually, we were just thinking of ways that we could make it more interesting and interactive. This is what we've planned, this is what you can expect in the session. So the first part will be very brief; it'll be about what has changed and how has it affected the counselor. The next part is going to be about the Letter of Reference, and the last part is going to be about the personal statement. In both the parts about the reference and the personal statement, we're going to keep format roughly similar: we're going to have a list of rapid-fire questions, then a case review, and then we're going to have like a debrief of the case review. So I hope you enjoy it. Next one, Bijoya. To start, what has changed in the UCAS application? Luckily, nothing much. Honestly, it's one of my favoritest applications. I think those of us who make college applications, most of us seem to love the UCAS application. It's simple, it's very straightforward, it can be done really easily by a student who's 17, 18. So, but the two changes that have come about is: one, the introduction of a structured three-question personal statement. Earlier, there used to be just one box with 4,000 characters and you had to fill in, and it was a bit of a challenge for a student to kind of figure it out. So that has been changed to three questions, and we'll share the three-question format soon. And the second one was the free-form reference letter, which has now again also been divided into three sections, and we'll talk about that. While these two things have changed, everything else has remained the same, including the 4,000-character limit. Let's go to the next. So, one of the things that we want to talk about right in the beginning is that with this change, actually—and the universities are going to talk about how it has impacted them—but I really want to talk about how it's impacted us or the counselor in the office. I'm in a school office, and I think for me, now the new personal statement, we've actually made worksheets out of it. It just gets stacks of it lying on my table, and any kid from grade 10th onwards who walks in, while they're waiting, they fill it in. It just, it's just something that is very, very useful. It serves as a diagnostic tool in terms of, you know, really what are the—what are the gaps, so to say, and also clarity building tool, which I found that, you know, when a kid says, "I love economics," and then they struggle with the first answer, what to put beyond the second point, it is quite revealing to the student themselves directly what that, you know, something is missing. So very, very useful inside the office. The divisions of sections of reference, I think, again, are very, very handy. So the way we do it in my school now is: Section A is definitely my work, so that's the context of the school, definitely done by me. The Section B, the extenuating circumstances, I would collaborate with the referee, with the teacher referee. And the Section C is written by the teacher and added by me. So again, it's become much more clearer because earlier we used to still do it this way, but it had to be, we had to kind of come up with a single statement, and now it's become very easy because we know who owns which part of the Letter of Reference. Bijoya, we can move to the next. So with that, I'll invite Mishi to take over the section about the Letter of Reference.

record.text: Product and fashion. Thank you so much, and that brings me to my next question to Miss Ritu. Uh Miss Ritu, if you're there on this, I wanted to understand which industry have you seen a rapid growth where creativity has played a vital role?

Juben Thakur: Absolutely. I think I think I very beautifully uh can sum up this that it's just not the brand, it's just the fit, you know, where where where student would want to be excelling and learning and being happy and translating the skills into into where the industry is leading right now. And that brings me to one of the beautiful questions. But I would like to share the screen since you highlighted about, you know, it's not about the university, it's more about the fitment. Let me quickly talk about some things in Leeds, which is very interesting. If you see my screen, there are a lot of Yorkshire Sculpture Park, and as I reiterated earlier as well, Leeds is a very beautiful and artistic city. It's very vibrant. It's very easy on students. It's very diverse. You know, it's it's very interesting if somebody wants to find artists and passion in them. This is one of the Kirkgate Market, which is wide known as the Leeds City Market. If if people know, Marks & Spencer was born in England, was born in Leeds, and that originated right at the bottom where you see the green gates. This is where Marks & Spencer as a brand was born in. And this is the legacy, Leeds City Market, where international students are exempted to go ahead and take the privilege of working 20 hours a week. And that's where a student usually goes because there are a lot of brands, there are a lot of shops inside where student can look for odd jobs in terms of hospitality. This is one of the Leeds Dock in the evening, which is right in the center of the city, where students do go ahead to unwind themselves in the evening. Talking about, you know, one of the most important things in design industry is networking. And that's exactly what we are doing right now to understand universities much better on one-on-one rather than these presentations to involve in conversations. I'm very proud to say that during my visit to Leeds as well, even I was clueless, but then I have started using this in my slides. We have something called as Leeds Digital Festival. I would give you a small homework as well before you go today. Please go ahead and type Leeds Digital Festival, or if you can go to Leeds Arts University campus tour, and if you can have a look at this 1-minute video about how our animation students has worked with graphics students and lit the entire city that came together to see the light show. There are very beautiful light shows that our students at Leeds Arts University do. Also not to forget that there are a lot of opera houses, one of the biggest opera houses, and every month, there's some sort of film festival happening at Leeds. So every student has the opportunity. I I would always say this to my student that not every time you'll get access to Aishwarya Rai and Shah Rukh Khans out there when they're there. But at least as a student, you can always walk up to the team, put in your resume, start networking, understand how this can really shape up your career. And also, we have one of the biggest festivals which is going on, which is called Leeds Concert. I think this is the industry that we're talking about, which is not depreciating. But every time there is always an increment not just to technology, but also UK as a as a wider community. I know there has been times where, you know, everybody has questions that, "Oh, there are no jobs in UK. You know, UK has gone down. UK has been like this, like that." But trust me, I was there at the last intake of this universities, and I am still there and I'm doing my second intake. The need and the want has not changed, although the circumstances of the countries have changed because of the policies, but the demand has never changed. And every country is still trying, especially UK as a design sector, is pumping nearly £104 to £160 billion in the creative careers. And that's why Leeds is not just becoming one of the most emerging universities, but the only specialist universities for those students. I'm I'm extremely proud to say this, that I know it could be a little biased, but I have to say this. But when I was there at the university for a span of week, I met 35 course leaders. I also met four higher education directors, the pro-vice-chancellor, the vice-chancellor of the university. And I I was surprised that I met a cohort of Indian students of first year, second year, third year, and final year students as well, and every faculty that I met, they knew my students' name. And it is as much as surprising to you as it was for me when I was there. But yes, we do know the name of each Indian students in the classroom, and we will talk more about this at the Q&A, because we do not have interviews just like other universities. We have uh our offers are made on the quality, not on the quantity of applications, and not just on the portfolios again. The course structure is very, very, very intensive. It's it's it's the orientation week that goes into the industry experts coming in and interacting with you, then you get familiarized with the technology. Then every year, there is end of the year show. The end of the year show for this year was called Big Bash Bosh. And also there are creative practices that we do. It's just not about the best portfolios to apply to the best schools. It's more about the process that needs in the design sector. Of all the people who have logged in right now, I can see that you do a lot of portfolio making, and everybody asks me, "Juben, what is a good portfolio?" I always tell my student, it's not about a good portfolio, but it's mere existence of your ideas into those beautiful structures. So I would like to see the versatility in your thought process from an idea to execution. I think that makes a portfolio and an interviewer to understand that you're open for possibilities. This is a screen for most of the educators out here, which you will realize the entry requirements is not that difficult. Because the university's existence is more about nurturing the creative brains. For a foundation students, it's minimum of 55%. For an undergraduate course is 65%. For most of you all dealing with the PG, it's nearly 55% in any graduation with the IELTS. Scholarship: we have a range of scholarships, specifically for Indian students. A minimum of £18,000—a minimum of £18,000 per year is the fee for undergraduate and postgraduate course. And also we offer a minimum of £2,000 scholarship. It could go more depending on the availability and the quality of the portfolio. This is something that I'm going to show you a little quick, because I really want to get into a little bit of question and answer, because dealing with the design industry is quite tricky, like Bhakti mentioned earlier, you know. So I would like to emphasize and throw some light on that as well. Some of the campuses, which you see state-of-the-art facility, helping students in public university to get printing and stationery for free. We also invest a lot of time getting students equipped to metal and wood workshops. Trust me, in India, it's considered to be a very, very non-organic growth, but that's not what international curriculum are designed for. We feel just because you're learning fashion doesn't mean you can get into fashion jobs. There are a lot of jobs in the metal industry that you can use your fashion tactics or use metal workshops in your industry with wood as well. Music studios, music performance, textile, auditorium, library. And before I jump to this beautiful exciting part that I show to my people, I also wanted to go ahead and wanted to understand from let me Miss Poonam. Miss Poonam, are you there in this session, if I may ask you?
